errorCodes.meaning: The request did not arrive on a mux connection, so there are no members' frames it could acknowledge. Send it on the connection the frames were delivered on.

AckRefusal.description: An id the mediator did not delete, and why.

reason.description: `notPermitted`: the message is held for a member this connection carries with the `receive` or `pickup` scope, which lacks the `delete` scope (or whose account no longer stands); it stays in the member's inbox. `notFound`: anything else — already deleted, expired, never delivered here, or held for a DID whose mail the connection cannot read (one it does not carry, or carries with neither `receive` nor `pickup`), which is not told apart from a message that does not exist.

AckRefusal.title: Ack refusal

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

MessageId.description: The lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of a stored message: for a TSP message, of the base64url (no padding) encoding of its qb2 bytes.
MessageId.title: Message id

Response.description: The success response to a messaging/mux/ack request: every requested id appears in `acked` or `refused`. Carried in a Trust Task document whose type is https://trusttasks.org/spec/messaging/mux/ack/0.1#response.

refused.description: Ids that were not deleted, each with its reason. Those messages are left as they were.
